title: Eviction trigger threshold desynchronization - incident follow-up and hardening
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: During a rolling config update to adjust eviction aggressiveness, a race in config propagation caused per-shard eviction thresholds to diverge from the controller policy. Some shards used the new lower free-space threshold while adjacent shards remained on the old setting, triggering repeated eviction-surges and subsequent KV cache compaction storms. This manifested as a capacity event (elevated OOM retries and request tail latency) for ~27 minutes across two regions.

Why this is different from prior incidents: previous incidents focused on checksum/poisoning and reference-count leaks. This event is a configuration desynchronization combined with feedback amplification from asynchronous compaction and stale telemetry, not a corruption bug.

Impact timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-01T09:02: config rollout began (canary shards)
- 2026-03-01T09:07: 3/12 shards in region-us-west switched to new threshold but metrics still reported aggregate free-space slowly
- 2026-03-01T09:12: eviction cycles escalated on updated shards; neighboring shards hit eviction pressure unexpectedly
- 2026-03-01T09:25: autoscale mitigations and emergency rollback triggered by on-call
- 2026-03-01T09:29: rollout paused and rollback completed; incident resolved by 09:40

Root cause hypothesis (consolidated):
1) Controller rollout sent threshold patch without a version-locked apply; agents apply the new value independently and emit metrics asynchronously.
2) Per-shard agent accepts partial config due to a timing window in the agent config apply path where default fallback was used when the controller message and local cache update interleaved.
3) The eviction heuristics use a combined global policy and a shard-local multiplier; when only one changed, the calculated threshold fell into a pathological region that aggressively evicted.
4) Compaction tasks are scheduled with exponential backoff but backpressure was insufficient; repeated compactions and eviction loops amplified memory churn.
5) Alerting thresholds were set on aggregate free-space and did not capture shard-level oscillation quickly enough.

Evidence:
- Correlated logs from runtime-agent (links below) showing config apply timestamps misordered with local cache refreshes.
- Shard-level free-space histograms showed a bimodal distribution starting at 09:07.
- PR benchmarks show new threshold reduces steady-state memory but enters oscillation for variance in request size > 3x normal.

Linked artifacts and telemetry:
- Incident runbook (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/KVCacheIncidents/931236
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv/shard-free-space?orgId=1&from=2026-03-01T09:00&to=2026-03-01T10:00
- Logs (runtime-agent): https://logs.redwood.ai/qry?incident=ENG-991236
- Rollout PR (revert/patch): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428

Action items (short-term, owners, ETA):
- A1: Add config versioning and atomic apply handshake between controller and agent. Owner: Diego Ramos. ETA: 2026-03-17. (AC: controller and agent exchange version IDs; agent rejects partial applies and logs an explicit failure metric.)
- A2: Introduce per-shard eviction-oscillation alerting (shard-level derivative on free-space + eviction-rate). Owner: Priya Nambiar. ETA: 2026-03-12. (AC: alert fires within 3m of sustained oscillation and creates a pager for P1.)
- A3: Tweak compaction scheduling to include a jittered leader election per-shard to avoid synchronized compactions; add backpressure circuit-breaker for compaction. Owner: Tomasz Kowalczyk. ETA: 2026-03-24. (AC: compaction retries limited and compaction concurrency < 2 per node under high load.)
- A4: Add an automated canary rollout that validates shard-level metrics before advancing global rollout. Owner: Maya Chen. ETA: 2026-03-20. (AC: rollout aborts automatically when shard variance exceeds threshold.)
- A5: Add unit/integration tests that model config race windows (simulate interleaved controller/agent updates). Owner: Eng QA. ETA: 2026-03-15. (AC: tests run in CI and catch the race for >= 3 simulated interleavings.)
- A6: Update runbook to include shard-level mitigation steps (scale down compaction workers, force consistent policy, emergency rollback). Owner: On-call rotation (Ops). ETA: 2026-03-10. (AC: runbook validated in next chaos drill.)

Longer-term proposals (research/engineering):
- L1: Replace local multiplier heuristic with a monotonic, versioned lease so threshold computation is deterministic across shards. Investigate trade-offs with latency and memory efficiency. Target: Q2 2026.
- L2: Add offline simulation harness to stress different rollout strategies against realistic traffic traces (used before any global config change). Target: Q3 2026.

Acceptance criteria for closure:
- All short-term action items (A1-A6) implemented or an explicit exception approved by the head of infra.
- Canary rollout exercised in production using a non-critical config patch and validated.
- New shard-level alerts and dashboards in place and exercised.

Risk and trade-offs considered:
- Stronger atomic config apply increases controller-agent coupling and slightly raises rollout latency; mitigated by asynchronous pre-flight checks and canary validation.
- More conservative compaction limits increase steady-state memory usage; we will tune during canary and ensure Dedicated customers can opt for more aggressive policies.

Communication plan:
- Notify impacted tenants and SREs with a short incident update and the mitigation plan by EOD 2026-03-02.
- Postmortem summary to be published to the infra-team channel and attached to the incident ticket after actions are closed.

Owners and escalation:
- Primary owner: Diego Ramos (runtime agent/config)
- Secondary: Priya Nambiar (observability)
- Escalation: Head of Platform (Liam O'Connor) if action items slip past due date by >7d
updates: 2026-03-01: Incident detected by SRE due to increased tail latency; on-call performed emergency rollback of recent eviction policy change.
2026-03-02: Initial RCA draft completed; identified config propagation timing window as likely contributor. Began drafting handshake design.
2026-03-04: Implemented temporary shard-level alert (non-pager) to surface oscillation; no further incidents observed during rollback window.
2026-03-08: Design review held (runtime, infra, SRE); consensus to pursue versioned config apply + canary gating. Action owners assigned.
2026-03-10: A1 PR opened for config-version handshake; tests added to CI that simulate interleaved updates.
acceptance_criteria: Atomic config handshake implemented and validated in staging
Shard-level eviction oscillation alerting triggers within SLO
Compaction backpressure implemented and verified under load
Canary rollout policy prevents immediate global rollout when shard variance is high
suggested_mitigation_steps: Pause rollout and rollback to previous policy (already executed during incident)
Force-compaction-worker-scale-down on affected nodes to break eviction loops
Apply temporary per-shard throttle to eviction if oscillation detected
Enable increased telemetry frequency for shard-level free-space during canary runs
